journal_articles.title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2-4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5-22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study-eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL-cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

journal_articles.title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons.
journal_articles.abstract: Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions1-4. Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches-Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification5 (831 neurons, 12 individuals)-showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7-46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10-6). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death6, whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

last_author.name: Christopher A Walsh

journal_articles.title: Long-read RNA sequencing identifies non-coding isoform switching as a regulator of cell fate.
journal_articles.abstract: Development of long-read RNA sequencing technologies has paved the way to the exploration of RNA isoform diversity and its relevance in regulating cell fate. However, identifying new functional isoforms is still very difficult. Here, we leverage long-read RNA sequencing to study changes in isoforms during somatic cell reprogramming and identify novel isoforms occurring throughout cell state transitions. We demonstrate tight regulation of non-coding isoforms and show that isoform switching plays previously overlooked functional roles and outcomes in gene regulation and cell fate changes. We uncover a novel long non-coding RNA, Snhg26, that undergoes isoform switching during reprogramming to enhance the conversion of differentiated cells towards the pluripotent state. Knock-down of Snhg26 in mouse and human pluripotency models reveals that it is important for pluripotency acquisition. Together, our study provides a resource to study full-length isoform usage during cell fate change. It also demonstrates the power of long-read sequencing to identify functionally relevant gene isoforms in the context of cell plasticity.

last_author.name: Samer M I Hussein

journal_articles.title: DR-GEM enables self-supervised machine learning for single-cell embeddings and annotations.
journal_articles.abstract: Dimensionality reduction and clustering are instrumental to single-cell and spatial genomics data analysis. Here we show that existing methods tend to fit oversampled classes and miss more unique signals and patterns, such as rare cell types and states. We find that the problem in such cases is not primarily data scarcity per se, but the model equating abundance with importance. Addressing this, we present "Distributionally Robust and latent Group-AwarE consensus Machine learning" or DR-GEM, a self-supervised meta-algorithm that uses the reconstruction error to reorient the model attention to patterns it initially missed and applies balanced consensus learning to increase robustness and filter low-quality data. We apply DR-GEM to synthetic and real-world single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, and Perturb-seq datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms existing methods in obtaining reliable embeddings, recovering rare cell types, filtering noise, mitigating cell-level and patient-level underrepresentation, and uncovering held-out genetic and spatial features. We thus surface and address an underappreciated problem and present a self-supervised framework to help support AI-based and data-driven discoveries.

journal_articles.title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium-derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

journal_articles.title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression.
journal_articles.abstract: Tandem repeats (TRs)-highly polymorphic, repetitive sequences across the human genome-are important regulators of gene expression but remain underexplored due to challenges in accurate genotyping and analysis1. Here we generate whole-genome and single-cell RNA sequencing from more than 5.4 million blood-derived cells across 1,925 individuals in two cohorts2, and perform meta-analysis to characterize the impact of variation in more than 1.7 million TR loci on immune cell type-specific gene expression. We identify more than 69,000 single-cell expression quantitative trait loci, 30.7% of which are specific to 1 of 28 immune cell types, and reveal dynamic regulatory effects using cell-state inference. Matched single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing profiles from more than 3.4 million nuclei in 922 individuals3 uncover chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci for nearly one-third of expression-associated TRs, supporting coordinated effects on cis-regulatory architecture. Fine-mapping implicates 1,490 TRs as candidate causal drivers of gene expression in 6.1% of tested genes, and colocalization analyses highlight more than 200 genes in which TRs likely mediate genetic associations with immune and haematological traits. Together, these results provide a genome-wide, multiomic view of TR-mediated regulation in the human immune system, establishing TRs as key contributors to cell type-specific regulatory variation and complex trait architecture.

journal_articles.title: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration.
journal_articles.abstract: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a (adma) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a, which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

last_author.name: Ching-Ling Lien

journal_articles.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation.
journal_articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle tissue underlies several polygenic metabolic traits and diseases. Identifying their genetic mechanisms requires pinpointing cell types, regulatory elements, target genes and causal variants. Here we use genetic multiplexing to generate population-scale single-nucleus chromatin accessibility (single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq)) and transcriptome (single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq)) maps across 287 frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies. We identify 13 cell types and integrate genetic variation to discover >7,000 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and >100,000 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) across cell types, including context-specific eQTL/caQTL with significant G × C interaction. We identify nearly 2,000 eGenes colocalized with caQTL and construct causal directional maps for chromatin accessibility and gene expression. Almost 3,500 genome-wide association study (GWAS) signals across 38 relevant traits colocalize with sn-eQTL/caQTL, most in a cell-specific manner. These signals typically colocalize with caQTL and not eQTL, highlighting the importance of population-scale chromatin profiling for GWAS functional studies. The results of this study illuminate the genetic regulatory architecture of human skeletal muscle.

last_author.name: Stephen C J Parker

journal_articles.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum.
journal_articles.abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

journal_articles.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets.
journal_articles.abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

journal_articles.title: Coordinated cell division and growth drive meristem notch formation in Ceratopteris gametophytes.
journal_articles.abstract: Meristems drive organogenesis and shape plant body plans, yet their morphology and cellular organization vary widely across land plants. Fern gametophytes develop a multicellular meristem that initiates at one flat margin of the prothallus and progressively forms a distinctive concave notch, producing the characteristic cordate gametophyte. Despite its importance for gametophyte growth and sexual organ formation, the cellular basis of meristem notch morphogenesis remains unclear. Here, we address this question in the fern Ceratopteris richardii using long-term time-lapse confocal imaging, chemical perturbations, and quantitative analyses at single-cell resolution. We reconstructed complete cell lineages and generated dynamic maps of cell division, size, growth rate, and collective cell displacement throughout development. Our analyses reveal that position-specific cell proliferation and division patterns, coordinated with differential cell expansion and dynamic cell displacement between the notch-forming lineage and adjacent wing regions, drive notch morphogenesis. Chemical perturbations disrupting microtubule function or cell-cycle progression disrupted notch formation, demonstrating that coordinated cell division and growth are required. Together, these findings establish a quantitative cellular framework for understanding meristem morphogenesis across land plants.

journal_articles.title: Immune-epithelial interactions orchestrate stem-cell niche formation and morphogenesis requiring TGF-β signaling.
journal_articles.abstract: Epithelial morphogenesis is generally attributed to mesenchymal and extracellular matrix interactions, whereas the role of immune cells in tissue assembly remains poorly defined. Here, we established a patient-derived, single-cell 3D hydrogel organoid system to examine immune-epithelial interactions during human mammary morphogenesis. CD45⁺ immune cells integrate into developing breast epithelial structures and persist throughout organoid formation, recapitulating their spatial organization in vivo. Functionally, immune cells act as instructive regulators in a donor-dependent manner, enhancing organoid number, branching, and proliferation. Reciprocal mixing experiments demonstrate that this phenotype is determined by the immune compartment, identifying distinct "inducer" and "non-inducer" states. Live imaging reveals that inducer immune cells undergo directed migration and establish stable early interactions with nascent epithelial clusters, whereas non-inducer cells fail to engage. Although inducer co-cultures produce a pro-morphogenic cytokine environment, soluble factors alone are insufficient to reproduce the phenotype. Instead, TGF-β signaling is required under these conditions, as pathway inhibition attenuates immune-driven morphogenesis whereas exogenous ligand is insufficient. These findings identify immune cells as essential, context-dependent regulators of enhanced epithelial morphogenesis in this organoid system.

last_author.name: Charlotte Kuperwasser

journal_articles.title: Loss of PAX6 alters the excitatory/inhibitory neuronal ratio in human cerebral organoids.
journal_articles.abstract: The transcription factor PAX6 is a crucial regulator of multiple aspects of embryonic forebrain development. It has well-established roles in the regulation of excitatory and inhibitory neuron development in the embryonic cortex in mice but PAX6's roles during human forebrain development are less well understood. Using human cerebral organoids, we investigated PAX6's roles in human neurodevelopment. Homozygous PAX6 mutant (PAX6-/-) organoids were larger than controls and contained increased inhibitory cell types. Excitatory neurons were still generated in PAX6-/- organoids but they were less mature, and a subset showed dysregulated expression of inhibitory identity genes compared to PAX6+/+ controls. The inhibitory cells found in PAX6-/- organoids physically segregated from excitatory neurons and presented a distinct transcriptomic profile when compared to in vivo cortical inhibitory neurons. PAX6-/- organoids showed a dysregulated cellular response to PTN-PTPRZ1 signalling, which contributed to the observed increase in inhibitory neurons and the consequent altered excitatory to inhibitory neuronal ratio.

journal_articles.title: The elongation of Mest transcript into MestXL sustains, but does not initiate, the maternal allele bias of its convergent gene Copg2 during neurogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Precise gene dosage control is critical for cellular identity and development, particularly for imprinted genes, where dosage imbalances are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders. The Mest/Copg2 imprinted locus exemplifies this fine-tuned regulation: while Mest is constitutively paternally expressed, Copg2 shifts from biallelic to maternally-biased expression specifically during neural differentiation, a transition proposed to involve transcriptional interference by the long Mest isoform, MestXL, which extends into Copg2. However, the mechanisms underlying this switch and whether factors beyond MestXL contribute remain unresolved. Using a stem cell-based brain organoid model integrating multi-omic analyses, 3D chromatin mapping, and functional approaches, we challenge the prevailing model by showing that the maternal bias of Copg2 is not solely driven by MestXL-mediated interference. Instead, our data reveal a temporal, stage-specific two-step mechanism: putative enhancer-driven activation of the maternal allele in neural progenitors, followed by MestXL-dependent repression of the paternal allele in neuron-enriched stages. This uncovers an unexpected complexity in imprinted gene dosage regulation during brain development.

last_author.name: Philippe Arnaud

journal_articles.title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity and plasticity are hallmarks of cancer that contribute to tumor growth and therapy resistance. Here, we investigated metabolic heterogeneity in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive cancer type with considerable plasticity between neuroendocrine (NE) and non-NE cellular states. Through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we identified a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine (Cys) across all NE/non-NE SCLC cell states. Notably, NE and non-NE cells with low ASCL1 transcription factor levels underwent ferroptosis upon Cys depletion, whereas ASCL1high cells underwent apoptosis while remaining resistant to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis resistance was driven by the direct transcriptional activation of GCH1 by ASCL1, resulting in increased levels of the antioxidants BH4/BH2. Accordingly, combined Cys depletion and inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts. These findings demonstrate that metabolic state influences cell-death susceptibility in SCLC and provide a rationale for therapeutic strategies that exploit these metabolic differences.

last_author.name: Julien Sage

journal_articles.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
journal_articles.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

journal_articles.title: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington's disease.
journal_articles.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT), yet how somatic repeat instability and HTT inclusions relate to selective cell loss in the human brain remains unclear. We have developed a multimodal spatial transcriptomics approach that enables the definition of transcriptional programs with subcellular resolution, somatic CAG repeat lengths, and eight other pathology markers, including HTT inclusions, in every cell of intact brain sections. Imaging 428,173 cells in the control and HD cortex revealed the selective vulnerability of layer 5-6 (L5-6) near-projecting (NP) neurons and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons, which undergo a >50% loss that is closely linked to large somatic repeat expansions (>450 ± 55 CAGs). Intranuclear inclusions were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions (250-350 CAGs) and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone. These data provide a comprehensive resource and establish a general framework for connecting repeat expansion and protein pathology across diverse cell types.

last_author.name: Don W Cleveland
last_author.affiliation: Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, University of California at San Diego, La Jolla, CA 92093, USA; Department of Neurosciences, University of California at San Diego, La Jolla, CA 92093, USA. Electronic address: dcleveland@health.ucsd.edu.

journal_articles.title: Mesothelial plasticity regulates lung mechanical homeostasis in regeneration and fibrosis.
journal_articles.abstract: Tissue mechanical adaptation is fundamental to organ development, regeneration, and disease, yet the cellular mechanisms that regulate tissue mechanical adaptation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that mesothelial cells are key regulators of lung mechanical adaptation. Following pneumonectomy, elevated stretch activates YAP (yes-associated protein 1) and induces a transient fibroblast-like mesothelial cell state (F-LMC) characterized by reduced mesothelial identity, increased fibroblast features, and extracellular matrix remodeling at the pleural surface. Yap deletion suppresses F-LMC formation, resulting in lung overinflation and defective regeneration following pneumonectomy. By contrast, in fibrotic lungs, this mesothelial remodeling program is aberrantly activated and restricts lung inflation. Inhibition of this maladaptive response prevents the decline in lung capacity following bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Collectively, our findings redefine the mesothelium as a mechanosensitive regulator of organ-scale mechanical adaptation and reveal how pleural surface remodeling controls tissue mechanics during regeneration and disease.

journal_articles.title: A three-dimensional human co-culture system reveals reciprocal embryo-endometrial adaptation at implantation onset.
journal_articles.abstract: Human embryo implantation begins with dynamic, tightly coordinated interactions between embryonic and endometrial compartments, yet the earliest trophoblast-endometrial interface dynamics remain poorly resolved in vivo. Here, using an endometrial assembloid-based three-dimensional co-culture system with human blastoids and natural blastocysts, we analyse implantation-like progression by time-series single-cell transcriptomics and functional perturbation. Importantly, we identify co-culture-induced trophoblast subsets marked by SDC1+MMP7+ and enriched for transcriptional features associated with extracellular matrix remodelling and cell migration. These subsets are reproducibly detected across independent implantation-like systems, emerge specifically within a decidualized stromal co-culture context, and are further linked to stromal-derived CSF3 signalling by intercellular communication analysis and targeted perturbation. In parallel, the endometrium displays transcriptional changes associated with enhanced decidualization and a glandular hypersecretory transition. Together, our study provides a tractable framework for dissecting reciprocal embryo-endometrial adaptation at the onset of implantation.

last_author.name: Yixuan Wang

journal_articles.title: Elevated ozone activates maternal immunity to drive offspring IgG-mediated anaphylaxis through IgG glycosylation alterations.
journal_articles.abstract: Global allergic disease burden is rising, driven by environmental factors like ozone (O3)-induced oxidative stress. Epidemiological studies have linked prenatal oxidative stress to offspring allergy susceptibility, but causality remains unproven. Here, our retrospective analysis including 5,299 pregnancies postulates that mid-to-late gestational O3 exposure triggers maternal immune activation (MIA), increasing neutrophil/monocyte abnormality risks. Using an animal model of prenatal O3 exposure-induced MIA, we demonstrate that offspring of MIA dams-especially males-exhibit heightened allergy susceptibility. Mechanistically, MIA disrupts maternal-fetal IgG transfer and neonatal glycosylation, particularly Mgat3-mediated N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) modifications. This perturbation preferentially activates juvenile male IL-17/TNF signaling. In adulthood, downstream transcription factors c-Jun/c-Fos activate Mgat4a to sustain GlcNAc glycosylation. This glycosylation of IgG is associated with enhanced IgG-FcγRIII affinity and more severe inflammatory responses during anaphylaxis. Our study bridges environmental epidemiology, immunology, and glycobiology to suggest how prenatal oxidative stress reprograms offspring immunity, offering insights into developmental origins of allergic diseases.

last_author.name: Nan Sang

journal_articles.title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply.
journal_articles.abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

last_author.name: Tatsuo Shibata
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory for Physical Biology, RIKEN Center for Biosystems Dynamics Research, Kobe, Japan. tatsuo.shibata@riken.jp.

journal_articles.title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential.
journal_articles.abstract: How do inflammation and activation of the regenerative genetic program affect intestinal epithelial cell behavior and shape responses to future injuries? Following injury, which typically induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) death, regeneration occurs via the proliferation of surviving ISCs and via cellular plasticity through dedifferentiation of progenitors and committed cells. While inflammation and cellular plasticity are hallmarks of regeneration, its long-term effects on epithelial cell behavior are not well understood. Using single cell multiomics, we demonstrate that inflammatory exposure and cellular plasticity imprint a lasting transcriptional and epigenetic memory on ISCs and their progeny, priming them for enhanced repair after subsequent injuries. Mechanistically, we identify IFN-γ as a critical driver of this primed regenerative state. These findings uncover how prior inflammation reprograms regenerative capacity, with implications for tissue resilience and disease susceptibility.

last_author.name: Jordi Guiu
last_author.affiliation: Cell Plasticity and Regeneration Group, Regenerative Medicine Program, Institut d'Investigació Biomèdica de Bellvitge-IDIBELL, L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain. jguiu@idibell.cat.

journal_articles.title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans.
journal_articles.abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

last_author.name: Vincent Pasque
last_author.affiliation: Department of Development and Regeneration, KU Leuven, Leuven, Belgium. vincent.pasque@kuleuven.be.

journal_articles.title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M3.I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M3.I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family-dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M3.I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

last_author.name: Mario Faretta

journal_articles.title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains.
journal_articles.abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662, a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

last_author.name: Johan Jakobsson

journal_articles.title: Collagen I-rich microenvironments influence cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis in stem cell-derived models of liver development.
journal_articles.abstract: Cholangiocyte dysfunction accounts for a substantial proportion of liver transplantations, yet progress towards regenerative therapies is limited by an incomplete understanding of the developmental cues that regulate human cholangiocyte specification and morphogenesis. Here, we established a defined culture system to investigate how collagen I influences hepatobiliary differentiation from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). Increased collagen I presentation was associated with a bias towards cholangiocyte specification, reduced hepatocyte identity and the formation of branched duct-like tubular structures. Similar effects were observed in primary human foetal hepatoblast organoids, indicating that collagen I-dependent lineage bias is conserved across independent model systems. Mechanistically, collagen I presentation was associated with activation of integrin α2β1- and YAP-associated signalling, while inhibition of collagen-integrin interactions impaired both cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis. Together, our findings support a role for collagen I-rich extracellular environments in human hepatobiliary differentiation and provide a defined experimental system for investigating extracellular matrix-dependent mechanisms of bile duct development in vitro.

journal_articles.title: The RNA-binding proteins Ddx6 and Ddx61 support development in mRNA-decay deficient pnrc2 mutants.
journal_articles.abstract: Somitogenesis is controlled by the segmentation clock, a molecular oscillator that controls periodic gene expression in unsegmented mesoderm and is regulated by a negative feedback loop driven by Hes/Her transcriptional repressors. In zebrafish, Pnrc2 is required for decay of her1 transcripts and additional oscillatory gene transcripts. Despite accumulation of numerous mRNAs, including those encoding developmental regulators, overt embryonic phenotypes are absent in pnrc2 mutants. Our previous work suggested that accumulated mRNAs are not translated in pnrc2 mutants, although the underlying mechanism(s) was unknown. We show here that many overexpressed transcripts in pnrc2 mutants have shortened poly(A) tails and are disengaged from ribosomes, and that deadenylation inhibition leads to somite defects in pnrc2 mutants. Transcripts encoding the P-body-associated protein Ddx61 are overexpressed and engaged with ribosomes in pnrc2 mutants, leading to an increase in Ddx61 protein that may compensate for the negative effects of transcript accumulation. Co-depletion of Ddx61 and Ddx6 in pnrc2 mutants increases her1 accumulation and leads to pleiotropic defects. Together, our results show that multiple post-transcriptional mechanisms ensure proper translation when mRNA decay is inhibited.

last_author.name: Sharon L Amacher

journal_articles.title: Blender tissue cartography: An intuitive tool for analyzing 3D microscopy data.
journal_articles.abstract: We present a powerful and user-friendly tool for tissue cartography, a 3D image analysis and visualization method that maps curved surfaces, like epithelial sheets, onto 2D projections. Volumetric microscopy can image complex 3D tissues, but 3D image data remains difficult to visualize and quantify. Many biological systems are organized as thin, curved sheets. Tissue cartography extracts and cartographically projects these curved surfaces from volumetric images. This converts 3D into 2D image data, facilitating visualization, analysis, and computational processing. Existing tools, however, demand advanced coding expertise and are limited to simple tissue geometries. Here, we describe https://nikolas-claussen.github.io/blender-tissue-cartography/blender tissue cartography (btc), an interactive add-on for the 3D editor Blender that makes tissue cartography user-friendly through a graphical interface and handles complex biological shapes through powerful computer graphics algorithms. An accompanying Python library supports faithful 3D measurements in 2D cartographic projections and custom analysis pipelines. Time-lapse data can be batch-processed by algorithmically aligning all time points to a single key frame. We demonstrate btc on diverse and complex tissue shapes from Drosophila, stem-cell organoids, Arabidopsis, and zebrafish. btc enables quantitative cartographic analysis of complex 3D tissues, broadening access to methods previously restricted to specialists, while leveraging tools from computer graphics to unlock new capabilities.

journal_articles.title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin.
journal_articles.abstract: The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding1,2. Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types3. However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and ARID1A deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites. ARID1A LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF-cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer-promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional Arid1a deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either Ctcf or Pbrm1 deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

journal_articles.title: NDE1-Mediated Regulation of Neural Progenitor Regional Identity and Its Implication in Microcephaly.
journal_articles.abstract: Despite their significance, the genetic and molecular bases of neurodevelopmental disorders remain poorly understood. In this study, using human brain organoids and mouse models, we show that loss of NDE1, a gene closely associated with microcephaly, disrupts progenitor identity, prolongs mitosis, and alters regional patterning in the forebrain. NDE1 knockout leads to a caudal identity shift of neural progenitor cells in the organoids and mouse brains, coinciding with aberrant ERK signaling. Notably, downstream activation of the ERK pathway restored rostral PAX6 expression in human brain organoids. Parallel analyses of Nde1 knockout mice confirmed disrupted regional patterning of the forebrain. Together, our data establish NDE1 as a critical regulator of early human brain regionalization and elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying the structural abnormalities observed in NDE1-associated microcephaly.

journal_articles.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy interferes with tertiary lymphoid structure formation in Epstein-Barr virus-associated gastric cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated gastric cancer (EBVaGC) is a molecularly distinct, highly immunogenic gastric cancer subtype, yet the role of tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) during therapy remains unclear. Using a large locally advanced EBVaGC cohort (144 samples), combined with spatial transcriptomics (11 samples) and a single-cell atlas (77 samples), we show that EBVaGC exhibits enhanced TLS formation compared with EBV-negative gastric cancer, with invasive-margin TLS (IM-TLS) predicting favorable prognosis. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy disrupts TLS formation and shows limited efficacy in EBVaGC. Recurrent tumors display increased neutrophil infiltration around TLS, with aging neutrophils recruited via the CXCR4-CXCL12 axis. Mechanistically, chemotherapy induces EBV reactivation, activating neutrophil pattern recognition receptors and promoting neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, which impairs lymphocyte migration and TLS maturation. These findings identify EBV reactivation-driven neutrophil aging and NET formation as a mechanism underlying poor prognosis in EBVaGC, positioning IM-TLS as a prognostic biomarker and neutrophil dysfunction as a therapeutic target.

journal_articles.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease.
journal_articles.abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

journal_articles.title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis.
journal_articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)-SE regulating IL1A, IL1B, and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE-centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

journal_articles.title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells.
journal_articles.abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

last_author.name: Gerd P Pfeifer

journal_articles.title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia.
journal_articles.abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2-frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies-directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2-mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

last_author.name: José Luis Sardina

journal_articles.title: Role of Leu and Val synthesis in sensing mitochondrial nutrient and energy availability.
journal_articles.abstract: How cells integrate nutrient availability to coordinate metabolism and growth remains poorly understood. Here, we identify branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) synthesis as a metabolic sensing system linking mitochondrial activity to translational and transcriptional control. Yeast limits Leu and Val import and instead relies on their synthesis, allowing BCAA production to reflect mitochondrial anabolic capacity. Reduced Val synthesis activates Gcn2, whereas reduced Leu synthesis inhibits TORC1, together decreasing translation efficiency and restricting growth. This response lowers levels of the transcriptional repressor Mig1, suppressing the Warburg/Crabtree effect and promoting alternative carbon source utilization. Remarkably, pharmacological inhibition of Leu/Val synthesis induces this metabolic reprogramming even in nutrient-rich medium, indicating that mitochondrial BCAA synthesis can partially override other nutrient-sensing pathways. Thus, BCAA synthesis couples mitochondrial anabolic capacity to Gcn2 and TORC1 activity and, through translational control of transcription factor abundance, shapes cellular metabolism.

journal_articles.title: A bioengineered intestinal epithelial-stromal model for studying coordinated epithelial migration during wound repair.
journal_articles.abstract: Fibroblasts reside underneath most epithelial tissues. In the intestine, recent studies have shown that fibroblast migration contributes to tissue morphogenesis and wound healing. Yet, whether physical interactions between epithelial cells and fibroblasts contribute to epithelial movement remains elusive. Here, we establish a reconstituted epithelial-stromal gap-closure model that enables the study of physical epithelial-fibroblast interactions during intestinal repair. Using this platform, we show that subepithelial fibroblast alignment enhances directed and persistent migration of organoid-derived intestinal epithelia. We demonstrate that direct contact with fibroblasts improves gap closure by promoting cell alignment, sustaining tissue integrity, and synchronizing crypt-villus migration. Fibroblasts undergo long-range ordering to align perpendicularly to the epithelial front and deposit protein paths that act as guidance features to direct epithelial migration. In parallel, epithelial cells acquire a wound-associated epithelial-like phenotype, but insufficient to explain the effects of fibroblast contact. Our findings uncover a dual role for intestinal fibroblasts in epithelial repair, coordinating both biochemical and physical cues to ensure efficient and cohesive migration.

last_author.name: Elena Martinez
last_author.affiliation: Biomimetic Systems for Cell Engineering Laboratory, Institute for Bioengineering of Catalonia (IBEC), The Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology (BIST), Baldiri Reixac 15-21, 08028 Barcelona, Spain.

journal_articles.title: Mechano-metabolic control of multicellular morphogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: During multicellular morphogenesis, tissues display mechanical behaviors reminiscent of non-living materials. Unlike inert matter, however, tissues are not shaped solely by external forces; they self-assemble by generating - and adapting to - internal forces, a process that requires active catabolic (energetic) and anabolic (biosynthetic) metabolism. Crucially, tissue mechanics can in turn instruct metabolic states, revealing a reciprocal relationship. In this Review, we first examine the central role of metabolism in controlling the mechanics of diverse morphogenetic processes. Moving beyond the simplistic view of metabolism as a ubiquitous supplier of energy and biosynthetic precursors upstream of mechanics, we highlight instead its tight spatiotemporal regulation and specificity in shaping particular aspects of tissue mechanics. We also discuss evidence for mechanical regulation of metabolism and propose in vivo systems in which similar mechanisms may operate. By focusing on the very properties that distinguish living materials from inert ones, research into mechano-metabolic feedback loops during multicellular morphogenesis has the potential to drive major advances in our understanding of developmental biology.

last_author.name: Alessandro Mongera
last_author.affiliation: Department of Cell and Developmental Biology, University College London, London WC1E 6BT, UK.

journal_articles.title: Modelling plant stem cells: evolution, development and regeneration.
journal_articles.abstract: In June 2025, The Company of Biologists Workshop 'Modelling Plant Stem Cells: Evolution, Development and Regeneration' brought together a diverse group of plant researchers to discuss open questions in plant developmental biology. Expertise ranged from computational modelling, cell biology and developmental genetics to paleontology. All participants shared an interest in understanding the establishment, maintenance and regeneration of plant stem cell niches, how these dictate plant growth and how stem cell niches arose through evolution. This led to fruitful discussions identifying necessary steps to further integrate experimental and computational approaches to speed up the transfer of knowledge from current model species to emerging model species. The discussion covered the evolutionary and practical aspects in the selection of plant model systems, the importance of both generalities and specificities of model systems and methodologies, and the use of computational models as tools to infer developmental mechanisms in emerging research species. The diversity in career stages of participants, the plant species used, and experimental versus computational approaches, created an environment for establishing cross-system and cross-disciplinary collaborations. Here, we present distinct ways to connect experimental and computational approaches, and discuss what is needed to foster hypothesis-driven collaborations, key for the emergence of integrative plant stem cell biology.

last_author.name: Renske M A Vroomans

journal_articles.title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated 'pseudobulk' counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

last_author.name: Joseph E Powell

journal_articles.title: SATB1 lowers the T cell receptor signaling threshold for thymocyte positive selection via super-enhancer reprogramming.
journal_articles.abstract: In early T cell development, thymocytes undergoing positive selection receive relatively weak T cell receptor (TCR) signals. However, the mechanisms by which thymocytes translate weak and transient TCR signals into lineage-defining transcriptional programs remain unclear. Here, we show that SATB1 plays a key role in enhancer activation during positive selection, as it promotes the expression of positive selection-associated genes by enhancing super-enhancer (SE) activation. Notably, SATB1 deficiency disrupts SE topological organization, weakens promoter-enhancer interactions, blunts TCR-induced Ca2+ signaling, and impairs the activation of positive selection genes such as Cd2 and Cd5, leading to defective CD4/CD8 lineage differentiation and abnormal premature thymocyte egress. Furthermore, SATB1 forms liquid-like nuclear condensates that act as scaffolds to build super-enhancer structures, stabilizing enhancer accessibility and enhancing enhancer-promoter interactions. Altogether, our findings suggest that SATB1 plays a crucial role in promoting positive selection by driving super-enhancer reprogramming and establishing enhancer-promotor interactions.

journal_articles.title: Spatial multi-omics reveals disease-associated oligodendrocytes and metabolic dysregulation in male Parkinson's disease mouse models.
journal_articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease involves progressive α-synuclein pathology, but how this reshapes the brain's spatial immunometabolic landscape, and how oligodendrocytes participate, remain incompletely defined. Here we combine single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and spatial metabolomics in male A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice across disease stages, together with male mice carrying adeno-associated virus-mediated α-synuclein overexpression, human midbrain and cerebrospinal fluid samples. We describe a disease-associated oligodendrocyte lineage marked by elevated Il33 and Kirrel3 that expands with pathology in both mouse models. Interleukin 33 is upregulated in oligodendrocytes and its receptor ST2 in microglia, and bidirectional manipulation of oligodendrocyte Il33 alters microglial ST2 activation, insoluble α-synuclein burden and motor performance. In the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area, transcriptomic and metabolomic changes converge on lipid- and glutamate-related pathways. Both proteins are also elevated in human Parkinson's disease midbrain and cerebrospinal fluid. These data implicate oligodendrocyte interleukin 33-ST2 signalling and provide a spatially resolved resource.

last_author.name: Wenlong Zhang

journal_articles.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity.
journal_articles.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation-based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

last_author.name: Weimin Ci
last_author.affiliation: Department of Urology, Chinese PLA General Hospital, Beijing 100039, China.

journal_articles.title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation.
journal_articles.abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

last_author.name: Po-Yen Chen

journal_articles.title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans.
journal_articles.abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O2) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1-up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1-driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

last_author.name: H Robert Horvitz
last_author.affiliation: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Department of Biology, Massachusetts Institute of Technology Cambridge, MA 02139, USA.

journal_articles.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
journal_articles.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

last_author.name: Nihal Altan-Bonnet
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory of Host-Pathogen Dynamics, National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (NHLBI), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Bethesda, MD, USA. Electronic address: nihal.altan-bonnet@nih.gov.

journal_articles.title: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis.
journal_articles.abstract: In animal-microbe symbioses, established symbionts are often thought to be confined to a niche and to lose motile appendages such as flagella. Whether this loss implies immobility within the host remains poorly understood. We report long-range, host-driven symbiont mobility in a dinoflagellate-acoel worm symbiosis. Using long-term tracking, fluorescence, and electron microscopy, we find that hundreds of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10-20 μm in size) travel across the body of an acoel worm host (Waminoa sp.) at around 1 μm/s while confined inside a network of ultra-thin (∼200 nm) host parenchymal cells. We show this mobility is driven by host actin machinery, with symbionts moving faster than comparable actin-based transport systems despite confinement. We further show spatiotemporal regulation of symbiont distribution during diel rhythms and regeneration. By characterizing an active, host-cytoskeleton-driven mechanism of symbiont transport, our work expands our understanding of the regulatory strategies by which holobionts maintain dynamic homeostasis.

last_author.name: Manu Prakash
last_author.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305, USA; Department of Oceans, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305, USA; Department of Biology, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305, USA. Electronic address: manup@stanford.edu.

journal_articles.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive.
journal_articles.abstract: DNA's anti-parallel structure presents a topological challenge to the replisome, as leading and lagging strands must be synthesized in opposite directions. How lagging-strand synthesis is coordinated with leading-strand synthesis remains unresolved in eukaryotes. To address this question, we directly visualized the dynamics of lagging-strand polymerases Pol α and Pol δ at active replication forks using single-molecule imaging in Xenopus nuclear extracts. Surprisingly, we find that neither Pol α nor Pol δ is stably tethered to the replisome. Instead, lagging-strand synthesis occurs distributively and entails the rapid recruitment of new molecules of Pol α and Pol δ for each Okazaki fragment. Consequently, leading- and lagging-strand synthesis are not intrinsically coupled. We propose that metazoans solve the problem of anti-parallel replication not by actively coordinating leading- and lagging-strand synthesis, but instead simply by recruiting new polymerases to synthesize each Okazaki fragment.

last_author.name: Gheorghe Chistol
last_author.affiliation: Chemical and Systems Biology Department, Stanford School of Medicine, Stanford, CA 94305, USA; Stanford Cancer Institute, Stanford School of Medicine, Stanford, CA 94305, USA; BioX Interdisciplinary Institute, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305, USA. Electronic address: chistol@stanford.edu.

journal_articles.title: BCLAF1 and responses to RAG-induced DNA breaks enforce pre-B cell checkpoint.
journal_articles.abstract: During early B cell development, pre-B cells encounter signaling from pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) and DNA damage responses (DDR) triggered by RAG-induced DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs) generated during immunoglobulin light chain (Igl) recombination. These signals drive cooperative and antagonistic programs to promote pre-B cell checkpoint. Here, we show in vivo that pre-B cells transition between distinct subpopulations predominated by either pre-BCR or RAG DSB-induced DDR signals. DDR initiates early in pre-B cells undergoing Igl recombination then drives cellular programming during terminal pre-B stages. We find that RAG DSB-induced DDR regulates coordinated pre-B cell differentiation, in part, by activation of the transcriptional repressor complex SPIC/BCLAF1. Loss of BCLAF1 disrupts pre-B cell developmental progression resulting in concomitant expression of pre-BCR and DDR programs with breakdown in segregation of clonal expansion and Igl recombination. These studies show that RAG DSB-induced DDR and BCLAF1 preserve pre-B cell checkpoint integrity in vivo during Igl recombination.

last_author.name: Jeffrey J Bednarski
last_author.affiliation: Department of Pediatrics, Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO, USA; Department of Pediatrics, University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. Electronic address: jeb683@pitt.edu.

journal_articles.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart.
journal_articles.abstract: Increasing evidence supports a pathogenic role for impaired energy metabolism in organ damage. Genetic diseases provide opportunities to investigate these mechanisms, as exemplified by Fabry disease (FD), caused by an α-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency and globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, with cardiomyopathy as the leading cause of death. Beyond Gb3 storage, impaired energy metabolism may contribute to cardiomyopathy. Here, we demonstrate mitochondrial dysfunction in FD heart and its therapeutic targeting. Using a humanized FD mouse model (R301Q-Tg/GLA knockout), embryonic fibroblasts, and neonatal and adult cardiomyocytes, we found impaired mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, increased reactive oxygen species, and a vicious cycle aggravating lysosomal dysfunction. These defects progressed with age, causing accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, energetic failure, apoptosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction. L-arginine, promoting NO/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial rescue, prevented cardiac abnormalities. Our findings identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of FD cardiomyopathy and reveal the lysosome-mitochondria axis as a targetable pathway in FD and beyond.

last_author.name: Guido Iaccarino
last_author.affiliation: Department of Clinical Medicine and Surgery, Federico II University, Naples, Italy; Interdepartmental Center of Research on Hypertension and Related Conditions (CIRIAPA), Federico II University, Naples, Italy. Electronic address: guiaccar@unina.it.

journal_articles.title: Embryonic reprogramming drives anaplastic transformation in thyroid carcinoma.
journal_articles.abstract: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a highly aggressive malignancy that often arises through anaplastic transformation of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Although genetic drivers such as BRAF and TP53 mutations are implicated, the mechanisms underlying this transition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that human ATC loses thyroid differentiation and acquires pluripotency-associated features, accompanied by MAPK pathway activation. Guided by parallels with induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming, we develop an in vivo reprogramming mouse model. Forced expression of Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM) induces anaplastic transformation of Braf-mutant thyroid epithelium even without Trp53 mutation, yielding an ATC-like phenotype that shares molecular and histological features with human ATC. A conventional Braf/Trp53-mutant model shows similar features. Reintroduction of NKX2-1 into human and murine ATC cells partially reverses embryonic reprogramming, suppresses proliferation and induces redifferentiation toward a PTC-like phenotype. Embryonic reprogramming is a central driver of anaplastic transformation and supports redifferentiation strategies.

last_author.affiliation: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Gifu University Graduate School of Medicine, Gifu 501-1194, Japan; Department of Otorhinolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Mie University Graduate School of Medicine, Tsu, Mie 514-8507, Japan. Electronic address: hirofumi-shibata@med.mie-u.ac.jp.

journal_articles.title: Heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3 deaminases to substitution and indel mutagenesis in lung adenocarcinoma.
journal_articles.abstract: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

last_author.name: John Maciejowski
last_author.affiliation: Molecular Biology Program, Sloan Kettering Institute, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY 10065, USA. Electronic address: maciejoj@mskcc.org.

journal_articles.title: IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines induce astrocyte programs that support antigen-dependent CD4+ T cell restimulation.
journal_articles.abstract: Astrocyte contributions to CNS antigen presentation remain poorly defined. We show that interferon gamma (IFN-γ, the sole type II interferon), with proinflammatory cytokines, induces astrocytes to express components mediating attraction of and antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells. Re-analysis of astrocyte-enriched single-cell sequencing from bacterial mimetic-injected mice revealed a transcriptionally distinct, IFN-responsive astrocyte population enriched for antigen-presentation genes 24 h after peripheral immune challenge. In vivo, type II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II+)GFAP+ astrocytes localize to the brain surface across multiple mouse models of neuroinflammation and in human neurological disease tissue. In vitro, purified astrocytes stimulated with IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines expressed MHC-II, costimulatory molecules, and lymphocyte-recruiting chemokines, and in co-culture supported rapid antigen-dependent expansion of previously activated CD4+ T cells. Human iPSC-derived CNS cultures showed equivalent induction of antigen-presentation machinery in human astrocytes following inflammatory cytokine stimulation. These findings define a cytokine-induced astrocyte state expressing antigen-presentation machinery at neuroimmune interfaces that can support local CD4+ T cell responses.
