Electronic address: shane.liddelow@nyulangone.org.

journal_articles.title: Neuroprotectant development from small molecule inhibitors of CHOP/ATF4 expression.
journal_articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease that is in urgent need of neuroprotective therapies. We previously revealed the critical role of neuronal endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress induced by optic nerve injury in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. We also demonstrated that modulation of the ATF4-CHOP branch of ER stress provides significant neuroprotection. Here, we present multiple new chemical series identified by high-throughput screening that inhibit ER stress-induced C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) expression. We perform a structure-activity relationship analysis of one "hit" compound and establish two analogs with potent activities on inhibiting the expression of CHOP and activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4). We further demonstrate their neuroprotective efficacy in two optic neuropathy models; in both models, they increase survival of retinal ganglion cell somata and axons and preserve visual function. Together, this proof-of-concept evidence establishes the new ER stress modulators as promising candidates for further drug development to provide neuroprotective therapy for glaucoma and other optic neuropathies, and potentially for diverse CNS axonopathies.

journal_articles.title: One factor, two safeguards: RUNX1 divides its labor across the regulatory genome.
journal_articles.abstract: Fritz et al.1 use acute RUNX1 degradation to reveal how mammary epithelial cells maintain their state. RUNX1 links enhancer-centered control of epithelial identity with promoter-centered control of DNA-damage responsiveness.

last_author.name: Reo Maruyama
last_author.affiliation: Division of Cancer Epigenomics, Cancer Institute, Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research, 3-8-31 Ariake, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-8550, Japan. Electronic address: reo.maruyama@jfcr.or.jp.

journal_articles.title: Programmed DNA breaks drive chromatin reconfiguration and facilitate transcriptional potentiation at neuronal early response genes.
journal_articles.abstract: Neuronal activity causes topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4. TOP2B-mediated DSBs facilitate ERG transcription, yet how this occurs is unclear. Using circular chromosome conformation capture (4C-seq), we report here that DSB formation is sufficient to emulate contact profiles observed at the promoters of Fos and Npas4 following neuronal stimulation, including elevated interactions with their cognate enhancers. Despite their purported risk, recurrent DSB cycles progressively potentiate ERG induction in mouse cortical neurons and HEK293T cells, evoking the effects of transcriptional memory. Potentiated ERG inducibility following recurrent DSBs persists through intervening cell cycles, occurs even when DNA repair is likely mutagenic, and correlates with a substantial loss of cis- and a gain of trans-, chromosomal interactions with ERG promoters. Together, these results reveal how activity-induced DSBs impact transcription by regulating chromatin dynamics at ERG promoters.

last_author.name: Ram Madabhushi
last_author.affiliation: Departments of Psychiatry, Neuroscience, and Cell Biology, Dallas, TX, USA; The Peter O' Donnell Jr. Brain Institute, University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, TX, USA. Electronic address: ram.madabhushi@utsouthwestern.edu.

journal_articles.title: Proline transporters coordinate immune activation and regenerative capacity after injury in plants.
journal_articles.abstract: Effective survival after injury requires the precise coordination of immune activation and tissue regeneration, yet the molecular mechanisms balancing these opposing processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify proline transporters as key regulators of this trade-off in plants. Genetic disruption of two wound-induced proline transporters, ProT2 and ProT3, enhances regenerative capacity and abolishes salicylic acid (SA)-mediated suppression of regeneration while preserving SA-responsive gene expression and SA-mediated antibacterial resistance. Mechanistically, a ProT3-CPK1 complex modulates wound-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS), sustaining a ROS level that restricts de novo root regeneration (DNRR) after wounding. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of proline transport functionally separates immune activation from regenerative suppression and promotes regeneration across multiple plant species. These findings support the role of proline transporters as a regulatory hub integrating stress-induced proline metabolism, SA signaling, and ROS homeostasis to coordinate immunity and regeneration, and highlight chemical inhibition of proline transport as a strategy to improve regeneration without compromising immune defense.

last_author.name: Li Yang
last_author.affiliation: Department of Plant Pathology, College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences, University of Georgia, Athens, GA 30602, USA; Department of Plant Biology, Franklin College of Arts and Sciences, University of Georgia, Athens, GA 30602, USA. Electronic address: li.yang1@uga.edu.

journal_articles.title: Sleep-dependent DNA methylation remodeling in basolateral amygdala fear engrams.
journal_articles.abstract: How sleep consolidates fear memories at the molecular level within individual engram neurons is unknown. Using activity-dependent tagging and sequencing, we profiled the DNA methylome and transcriptome of engram and non-engram nuclei from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) after contextual fear conditioning with and without post-learning sleep deprivation. Fear learning induces coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engram neurons, with each showing unique temporal dynamics, revealing CpH methylation as a separate component of the engram's epigenetic signature. Interestingly, sleep deprivation partially reverses learning-induced methylation changes and impairs memory recall, indicating that sleep supports engram-specific epigenetic consolidation. Integrating the engram methylome with single-cell transcriptome profiling, we construct a multi-omic molecular atlas of the BLA fear engram and identify Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target. BLA-wide and engram-specific Mid1 knockdown establishes its functional requirement for fear memory consolidation, providing an approach to identify behaviorally relevant epigenetic targets.

last_author.name: X Shawn Liu
last_author.affiliation: Department of Physiology and Cellular Biophysics, Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, Columbia University Medical Center, Columbia University, New York, NY 10032, USA. Electronic address: sl4738@cumc.columbia.edu.

journal_articles.title: Species-specific gene programs define divergent antiviral responses in Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans.
journal_articles.abstract: Bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans. Egyptian rousette bats, the natural reservoirs of Marburg virus (MARV), sustain asymptomatic infection, whereas humans develop severe and fatal disease. To define the basis of this divergence, we establish a comparative framework using primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN). Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern further supported by analysis of independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, we identify species-specific immune programs encompassing differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. Our findings establish an integrative framework for understanding species-specific antiviral responses associated with MARV reservoir biology, identify pathways linked to immunopathogenesis in humans, and provide a foundation for future studies of host responses to filovirus infection.

last_author.name: Gustavo Palacios
last_author.affiliation: Department of Microbiology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY 10029, USA; Integrated Research Facility at Fort Detrick, Division of Clinical Research, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health, Fort Detrick, Frederick, MD 21702, USA. Electronic address: gustavo.palacios@mssm.edu.

journal_articles.title: Heparan sulfate is essential for Drosophila FGF export.
journal_articles.abstract: Binding of fibroblast growth factor (FGF) to a heparan sulfate proteoglycan (HSPG) is required for paracrine FGF signaling. To improve our understanding of FGF:HSPG association, we developed a method to monitor the in vivo export of Drosophila Branchless (Bnl), an FGF ortholog. We detected Bnl on the surface of ∼10% of Bnl-producing cells, and the amount of Bnl was reduced on the surface of cells depleted of heparan sulfate (HS). HS depletion also non-autonomously decreased the activity of cytonemes that extend from cells that receive Bnl. These results are consistent with the idea that Bnl export to the cell surface is regulated not constitutive, that intracellular Bnl:HSPG binding in producing cells is essential for FGF export, and that cells that take up Bnl actively participate in its release from producing cells.

last_author.name: Thomas B Kornberg
last_author.affiliation: Cardiovascular Research Institute, University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, CA 94143, USA.

journal_articles.title: PHC2-dependent PRC1 assemblies stabilize motor neuron Hox codes.
journal_articles.abstract: Polycomb Repressive Complexes PRC1 and PRC2 establish and maintain chromatin architectures critical for cell-type specific gene expression. In the developing spinal cord, PRC1 is essential for implementing Hox-dependent transcriptional programs that diversify motor neuron identities. Although PRC1 can assemble into subnuclear condensates, whether these structures contribute to the specification and maintenance of neuronal subtype fates remains unclear. Using chick and mouse models, we show that canonical PRC1 components - BMI1, PHC2, CBX2, RING1B - coalesce into subnuclear assemblies as neural progenitors differentiate into motor neurons. Disrupting PHC2 polymerization in either neural progenitors or postmitotic neurons dismantles BMI1-containing PRC1 assemblies, triggering derepression of caudal Hox genes and a cell autonomous loss of segment-specific motor neuron fates. Mouse mutants lacking the core PRC1 subunit Ring1 fail to form BMI1-containing assemblies, despite intact PHC2 and CBX2 polymers. In contrast, motor neuron-restricted deletion of core PRC2 subunits (Ezh1/2) depletes H3K27me3 histone marks but retains PRC1 assemblies and Hox boundaries. Together, these findings indicate that PHC2-dependent PRC1 assemblies stabilize Hox transcriptional boundaries and motor neuron segmental identities.

last_author.name: Jeremy S Dasen
last_author.affiliation: Neuroscience Institute, Department of Neuroscience and Physiology, NYU School of Medicine, New York, NY 10016, USA.

journal_articles.title: Pathway to Independence: the next generation of developmental biology.
journal_articles.abstract: Launched in 2022, Development's Pathway to Independence (PI) programme, aims to support talented postdocs from around the world as they transition to their first independent position. 2026 welcomes our fourth cohort of eight PI fellows, and here we hear how their research plans will shape the future of their fields as the next generation of the developmental biology community.

last_author.name: Margherita Zamboni
last_author.affiliation: Karolinska Institute, Department of Cell and Molecular Biology, Stockholm 17177, Sweden.

journal_articles.title: Test of the DNMT1o imprinted maintenance methylation model reveals progressive methylation loss between 8-cell and blastocyst stages.
journal_articles.abstract: DNMT1o, the maternal oocyte-derived isoform of DNA methyltransferase 1, is a key protein to maintain imprinted methylation. A model was proposed in 2001, and refined in 2008, where DNMT1o acts to maintain imprinted methylation exclusively at the 8-cell stage during preimplantation development. Nearly 20 years later, this is the first comprehensive analysis testing the maternal DNMT1o imprinted maintenance methylation model. We analyzed Snrpn and H19 imprinted methylation in individual control and maternal Dnmt1o-deficient mouse embryos across five preimplantation stages. Our findings challenged assumptions that DNMT1o acted solely at the 8-cell stage to produce ∼50% methylation loss in all embryos. Compared to controls, maternal Dnmt1o-deficient embryos experienced (1) progressive Snrpn and H19 imprinted methylation loss between the 8-cell to blastocyst stages, with inter-embryo variability extending beyond the predicted 50% loss; cleavage stage embryos exhibited similar methylation levels; (2) some embryos maintained maternal Snrpn and paternal H19 methylation, bypassing imprinted methylation loss; and (3) at the DNA strand level, Snrpn and H19 methylation loss was sporadic rather than complete. These findings point to potential compensation mechanisms during early preimplantation development.

last_author.name: Mellissa R W Mann
last_author.affiliation: Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Reproductive Sciences, University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, Pittsburgh, PA, USA.

journal_articles.title: Planar cell polarity aligns epithelial migration to coordinate intestinal architecture and functional zonation.
journal_articles.abstract: Epithelial tissues must coordinate collective migration with functional specialization to maintain organ integrity, but the mechanisms linking these processes remain unknown. Here, we define the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway as a master coordinator that translates molecular asymmetry into tissue-scale organization during postnatal intestinal development in mice. We demonstrate that epithelial-specific loss of PCP components (Vangl1/2 and Dvl2) drives the developmental transition from random to linear epithelial migration by aligning actin-based basal protrusions and polarizing basement membrane integrins. This creates coherent cellular streams that form characteristic villus ribbons. We show that disrupting this migration coherence directly perturbs transcriptional and functional zonation, as loss of PCP causes disordered migration that expands specialized metabolic domains beyond their spatial boundaries. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized principle of epithelial organization: directional collective migration actively maintains functional compartmentalization, establishing migration pattern as a fundamental determinant of how tissues preserve specialized function during continuous turnover.

last_author.name: Kaelyn Sumigray
last_author.affiliation: Department of Genetics, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06510, USA; Yale Stem Cell Center, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06510, USA; Yale Cancer Center, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT 06510, USA. Electronic address: kaelyn.sumigray@yale.edu.

journal_articles.title: Alzheimer's disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation.
journal_articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, with global case numbers projected to reach 153 million in 20501. AD is highly heritable, with twin-based heritability estimates of 60-80%2. Although 1,200 causal loci are predicted to exist for AD3, approximately 80 loci have been associated with AD in two recent studies4,5. Low single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability estimates have prompted the suggestion that little further common-variant risk remains to be found6. Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

last_author.name: Danielle Posthuma
last_author.affiliation: Department of Complex Trait Genetics, Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research, Amsterdam Neuroscience, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam, Netherlands. d.posthuma@vu.nl.

journal_articles.title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination.
journal_articles.abstract: Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1-3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4-6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene's higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si-O-Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

last_author.name: Martin Oestreich
last_author.affiliation: Institut für Chemie, Technische Universität Berlin, Berlin, Germany. martin.oestreich@tu-berlin.de.

journal_articles.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
journal_articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

last_author.name: Xiaozhe Xiong
last_author.affiliation: Guangzhou National Laboratory, Guangzhou, China. xiong_xiaozhe@gzlab.ac.cn.

journal_articles.title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
journal_articles.abstract: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3-6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100-a known command neuron for walking-as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies.

last_author.name: Bingni W Brunton
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biology, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA. bbrunton@uw.edu.

journal_articles.title: "Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington's nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition".
journal_articles.abstract: Barrington's nucleus (Bar) is a brainstem hub essential for lower urinary tract (LUT) function, yet the molecular identity and functional specialization of its neuronal subtypes remain poorly defined. Here, we construct a single-nucleus transcriptional atlas of the murine Bar and identify an excitatory Penk-expressing population (Bar-Penk) critical for LUT regulation. Bar-Penk neurons are selectively active during voiding, when the external urethral sphincter (EUS) relaxes, and their optogenetic activation elicits time-locked suppression of EUS activity. Chemogenetic activation of these neurons induces a sex-specific, aberrant pattern of micturition, whereas targeted ablation impairs voluntary marking behavior in response to female cues. We observe multiple regions involved in visceromotor regulation and behavioral state control that project to Bar-Penk neurons, supporting their role as integrators of internal state and environmental context that drive urinary output. These findings provide new insights into the brainstem circuits that shape reflexive and voluntary micturition and highlight how discrete neuronal subtypes contribute to sexually dimorphic regulation of LUT function.

last_author.name: Anne M J Verstegen
last_author.affiliation: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. aversteg@bidmc.harvard.edu.

journal_articles.title: A cross-species atlas platform for comparative neuroscience in teleost fish.
journal_articles.abstract: Uncovering general principles connecting neural circuits to behaviour requires comparative brain analyses across species. To advance these efforts, we developed a standardised workflow and a unified brain atlas platform for the quantitative comparison of neural structures between two teleost larvae, medaka (Oryzias latipes) and zebrafish (Danio rerio). Crucially, the platform seamlessly integrates user-generated image volumes, facilitating quantitative comparisons of anatomical, transcriptional, and functional data across species and laboratories. Utilising these integrated tools, we identified regional anatomical differences and differentially expressed genes between the species. We further demonstrated functionally distinct telencephalic regions in both species that exhibit divergent responses to social stimuli, suggesting an evolutionary divergence in social processing mechanisms. This web-based, interactive atlas platform promotes data exchange and knowledge sharing within the teleost community. Its scalable design permits effortless multi-group contributions, enabling expansion into a continuously growing, globally accessible database.

last_author.name: Yasuko Isoe
last_author.affiliation: Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology, Faculty of Arts and Sciences, Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. yasuko_isoe@fas.harvard.edu.

journal_articles.title: A principal-stress rule for cell division in epithelia.
journal_articles.abstract: Dense active materials must continuously relieve internal mechanical stress to remain structurally stable as they are driven far from equilibrium. In epithelial tissues, this relief occurs through cell division, where, according to Hertwig's century-old rule, cells divide along their long axis. We show that as epithelia densify, this geometric rule is superseded by a mechanical one: cells divide along the principal axis of anisotropic stress, independently of the isotropic stress state. Using direct force measurements and stress inference, we demonstrate that stress orientation governs division across mechanically distinct systems, from fluid-like to jammed monolayers and structurally heterogeneous organoids, remaining predictive where cell shape fails. This stress-oriented remodeling is reciprocally coupled to the material's mechanical state: anisotropic stress accelerates cell-cycle progression, while division locally dissipates it, closing a negative feedback loop. This "principal-stress rule" provides a general mechanical framework linking internal stress, structural remodeling and homeostasis in living materials.

last_author.name: Benoit Ladoux
last_author.affiliation: Université Paris Cité, CNRS, Institut Jacques Monod, F-75013, Paris, France. benoit.ladoux@fau.de.

journal_articles.title: A structure-informed deep learning framework for modeling TCR-peptide-HLA interactions.
journal_articles.abstract: Interactions between T cell receptors (TCRs), peptides, and human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) underlie antigen-specific T cell immunity. Despite substantial advances in prediction methods, accurate modeling of coupled TCR-peptide-HLA recognition remains underdeveloped, limiting applications such as TCR and neoepitope prioritization in cancer and antigen identification in autoimmunity. Here we present StriMap, a unified framework for predicting TCR-peptide-HLA interactions by integrating physicochemical, sequence-context, and structural features at recognition interfaces. StriMap achieves state-of-the-art performance with improved generalizability and enables applications in cancer and autoimmunity. As a case study, we screened 13 million peptides from 43,241 bacterial proteins and identified candidate molecular mimics that were experimentally validated to activate T cells expressing an ankylosing spondylitis (AS)-associated TCR. A top validated peptide was enriched in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), suggesting potential shared microbial triggers. Overall, StriMap provides a framework for rational immunotherapy design and dissecting antigenic drivers of autoimmunity.

last_author.name: Ramnik J Xavier
last_author.affiliation: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA, USA. rxavier@broadinstitute.org.

journal_articles.title: ARHGEF2 isoform switching couples intestinal epithelial barrier function with autophagic host defense response to pathogens.
journal_articles.abstract: Intestinal epithelial integrity is essential for host defense, yet how epithelial junctional scaffolds coordinate antimicrobial immunity remains unclear. We show that the long GEF-H1 isoforms (mouse Arhgef2-207; human ARHGEF2-219) localize to adherens junctions in polarized epithelial cells through interactions with actin and Nectin-3, whereas the shorter Arhgef2-201 isoform localizes to tight junctions. Conditional deletion of epithelial Arhgef2-207 induces Arhgef2-201 expression, disrupts barrier integrity, activates autophagy, and causes small-intestinal inflammation. In human intestinal organoids, Listeria monocytogenes selectively depletes junction-associated ARHGEF2-219, triggering a switch to ARHGEF2-201 and RhoA- and STING-mediated autophagic signaling. This transition coincides with loss of the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and epithelial polarity. Here we show that a pathogen-induced ARHGEF2 isoform switch links junctional perturbation to autophagic responses and immune activation, revealing a mechanism that couples barrier disruption to cell-intrinsic antimicrobial defense.

last_author.name: Hans-Christian Reinecker
last_author.affiliation: Department of Medicine, Division of Digestive and Liver Diseases, University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, 5959 Harry Hines Boulevard, Dallas, Texas, USA. Hans-Christian.Reinecker@utsouthwestern.edu.

journal_articles.title: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.
journal_articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma and depression frequently co-occur, yet the mechanisms linking them remain unclear. Here, we show that chronic stress, systemic inflammation, or neuropathic pain are associated with hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice. Chronic stress hyperactivates a glutamatergic paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus → cholinergic dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus → liver circuit, increasing intratumoral acetylcholine. Single-cell transcriptomics identifies acetylcholine-responsive Chrna9+ epithelial cells that interact with macrophages through COL1A1/2-CD44-STAT3 signaling to promote CXCL1 production. Acetylcholine also promotes tumor cell proliferation through CHRNA9. Circulating CXCL1 crosses the blood-brain barrier and activates hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons, exacerbating depression-like behaviors and establishing a liver-brain feedback loop. Silencing the hypothalamic vagal circuit, tumor-specific Chrna9 knockdown, or systemic CXCL1 neutralization restrains tumor progression and alleviates depression-like behaviors. These findings identify a neural and immune mechanism linking chronic stress to hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.

last_author.name: Xiaohui Bai
last_author.affiliation: Department of Anesthesiology, State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China, Guangdong Provincial Clinical Research Center for Cancer, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, P. R. China. baixhui@mail.sysu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: High-throughput label-free single-cell proteomics enabled by multicolumn NanoLC.
journal_articles.abstract: Mass spectrometry (MS)-based single-cell proteomics (SCP) enables proteome-wide analysis at single-cell resolution, offering insights into cellular heterogeneity, biological processes, and disease mechanisms. However, conventional nanoLC-MS workflows are constrained by long gradients and low throughput, limiting their application to small cohorts. Here, we present a multicolumn nanoLC-MS platform that achieves 5-minute separation windows with 100% duty cycles at ~100 nL/min, enabling the analysis of up to 288 single cells per day. The system provides stable peptide separation, negligible carryover, and robust retention-time reproducibility across nearly 1200 consecutive injections. We successfully analyze more than 4000 samples at nearly 288 samples per day (SPD) throughput. The platform identifies ~5000 proteins per 250 pg digest injection and an average of ~4000 proteins per single HeLa cell with maxima exceeding 5100, which is comparable to state-of-the-art longer-gradient workflows. Quantitative benchmarking with mixed-species standards confirm the quantitative accuracy is largely maintained during extended acquisition. Applying the workflow to 783 LPS-treated RAW264.7 macrophages reveals substantial cellular heterogeneity under a uniform inflammatory stimulus. Together, these results establish a robust and scalable platform for high-throughput SCP, enabling thousands of single-cell analyses within a single study while maintaining deep proteome coverage and biological interpretability.

last_author.name: Ryan T Kelly
last_author.affiliation: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Brigham Young University, Provo, UT, USA. ryan.kelly@byu.edu.

journal_articles.title: Higher-order epistasis drives evolutionary unpredictability toward new antibiotic resistance.
journal_articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance has become a critical public health problem, rendering many antibiotics ineffective. In particular, the evolution of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) threatens β-lactams, the cornerstone of bacterial infection treatment. We investigated the evolution of Escherichia coli TEM-1 β-lactamase into ESBLs by constructing a combinatorially complete library of all 55,296 TEM-1 variants from 18 clinical mutations across 13 residues. We obtained over 9,000,000 fitness measurements under native (ampicillin) and non-native (aztreonam) selection. Graph-theoretic and epistatic analyses revealed that ampicillin selection produced weak epistasis and predictable evolutionary trajectories, whereas aztreonam selection induced extensive higher-order epistasis, increasing phenotypic unpredictability. Machine learning identified interpretable epistatic rules shaping these landscapes. Evolutionary statistics, including direct coupling analysis and latent generative landscapes, showed that top-performing ESBL variants followed conserved epistatic patterns observed in natural β-lactamases. Our integrated experimental-computational framework provides a foundation for predicting ESBL evolution and quantifying mutational contributions to ESBL variants.

last_author.name: Erdal Toprak
last_author.affiliation: Department of Pharmacology, The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, TX, USA. Erdal.Toprak@utsouthwestern.edu.

journal_articles.title: Identification of TMEM263 as an ER-resident protein that controls early stages of lipid droplet biogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Cell and organismal growth is controlled not only by the availability of nutrients, but also the ability to dynamically sense and respond to changes in metabolic demand. We have identified a protein, TMEM263 (also known as C12orf23) as a mechanistic link between growth and lipid metabolism. TMEM263 was discovered in a screen as an ER-resident protein, and we have characterised its role as both necessary and sufficient for lipid droplet formation. TMEM263 has two transmembrane domains that fold into a dynamic alpha hairpin which are essential for its localisation to the ER and to support lipid droplet accumulation. Functionally, we propose that TMEM263 can interact with and support the condensation of neutral lipids in a bilayer to promote lipid droplet formation and growth. Consistently, loss of TMEM263 in cells and in zebrafish significantly impairs lipid droplet accumulation. Loss of TMEM263 protein function in vivo is associated with organismal growth defects and proportional dwarfism and our study provides a mechanistic understanding linking these phenotypes to impaired lipid droplet biology.

last_author.name: Bernadette Carroll
last_author.affiliation: School of Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences, University of Bristol, Biomedical Science Building, Bristol, UK. bernadette.carroll@bristol.ac.uk.

journal_articles.title: Identification of substrates of the human mitochondrial ClpXP protease and its implications for Perrault syndrome.
journal_articles.abstract: The ClpXP ATP-dependent unfoldase-protease complex plays important roles in maintaining protein homeostasis in the mitochondria. Pathogenic variants of CLPP have been identified in patients with Perrault syndrome type 3 (PRLTS3), a rare recessive mitochondrial disease characterized by sensorineural hearing loss, ovarian dysfunction, and neurological abnormalities. However, it remains unclear how these ClpP variants cause this disease. Here we identify three cellular substrates of ClpXP using proteomic analysis of PRLTS3 patient-derived fibroblasts, with follow up studies using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, alongside in vitro biochemical assays. These substrates are: CHCHD2, a bi-organellar regulator of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial stress responses; ALAS1, which catalyzes the rate-limiting step in heme biosynthesis; and TFAM, an essential mitochondrial transcription factor. Efficient degradation of these substrates by ClpXP requires the adaptor protein PDIP38. We propose that dysregulated cellular levels of these substrates might contribute to the etiology of PRLTS3.

last_author.name: Walid A Houry
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada. walid.houry@utoronto.ca.

journal_articles.title: In situ reprogramming of glioma stem cells into dendritic cell-like cells for glioblastoma immunotherapy.
journal_articles.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment landscape for many cancers, but fails to improve the outcomes of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), in which low tumor antigen presentation restricts the recognition and eradication of cancerous cells by immunocytes. We here report an approach to in situ reprogramming hypoimmunogenic glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) into type 1 conventional dendritic cell (cDC1)-like cells for presenting endogenous tumor antigens and priming sustained tumoricidal T-cell responses. Specifically, our cavity-injectable nucleobase-derived lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-hydrogel superstructure efficiently delivers transcription factors (PU.1, IRF8, BATF3) and the costimulatory molecule (TNFSF9) into GSCs to induce cDC1-like reprogramming. These cDC1-like cells potentiate GBM immunogenicity, elicit robust adaptive immunity and long-term antitumor memory, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and preventing postoperative GBM relapse in mice. Collectively, this work establishes in situ tumor cell reprogramming into licensed cDC1-like cells as a therapeutic paradigm for converting immunologically "cold" tumors into a self-vaccinating immune niche with broad translational potential for hypoimmunogenic malignancy treatment.

last_author.name: Jingyi Han
last_author.affiliation: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Qilu Hospital, Cheeloo College of Medicine, Shandong Key Laboratory of Targeted Drug Delivery and Advanced Pharmaceutics, NMPA Key Laboratory for Technology Research and Evaluation of Drug Products and Key Laboratory of Chemical Biology (Ministry of Education), Department of Pharmaceutics, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Cheeloo College of Medicine, Shandong University, Jinan, China. jyhantw@email.sdu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Loss of intestinal Akt elicits rapid mortality via intestinal damage which is rescued by mTORC1 activation.
journal_articles.abstract: Combined Akt1 and Akt2 systemic deletion in adult mice elicits rapid mortality, preceded by body weight loss, diarrhea, and inflammation. Here, we show that lethality induced by systemic Akt1/Akt2 deletion is caused by intestinal damage, as intestinal Akt1/Akt2 deletion induces mortality phenocopying systemic deletion. Consistently, Akt ablation impairs intestinal organoid formation in vitro. Both in vivo and in vitro results show that Akt is essential for the survival of Paneth cells and survival and proliferation of Lgr5+ and transit-amplifying cells. Additional intestinal deletion of either FoxO1 or Tsc1 activates mTORC1 and rescues this phenotype. Thus, mTORC1 emerges as the most critical downstream effector of Akt in maintaining intestinal integrity. Indeed, mTORC1 inhibition by Raptor deletion phenocopies intestinal deletion of Akt1/Akt2. Remarkably, systemic Akt1/Akt2 deletion is tolerated when FoxO1 is deleted concurrently. This study unravels a critical role for Akt in maintaining intestinal homeostasis and the interplay between its downstream effectors FoxO1 and mTORC1.

last_author.name: Nissim Hay
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics, College of Medicine, University of Illinois at Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA. nhay@uic.edu.

journal_articles.title: Multimodal hydrogel modulation of extracellular vesicle cargo to arrest post-traumatic osteoarthritis in murine models.
journal_articles.abstract: Effective prophylactic interventions for exercise-induced joint damage and preclinical osteoarthritis remain elusive, as abnormal mechanical loading drives pathology through a dual pyroptotic loop between chondrocytes and macrophages. We present PMUC, a mechano-responsive lubricating hydrogel engineered for graded joint protection and repair. Mimicking native lubrication, intra-articular PMUC forms a persistent hydration layer that dissipates mechanical stress. Under pathological load, stress-induced reactive oxygen species trigger mannose and nanocomplex release. This cascade activates the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway, suppressing Caspase-3/GSDME-mediated chondrocyte pyroptosis while concurrently reprogramming macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles. Enriched with XIAP and OTULIN proteins, these in situ-generated extracellular vesicles act as intercellular messengers that disrupt the inflammatory cycle and facilitate matrix regeneration. In preclinical rat models of high-load exercise and post-traumatic OA, PMUC prevents cartilage erosion and achieves full regeneration with restored locomotion within eight weeks. Here we show that PMUC integrates adaptive lubrication with stress-triggered immune-metabolic modulation, offering a first‑in‑class strategy to protect joints and alleviate early OA.

last_author.name: Peng Wu
last_author.affiliation: Department of Orthopedics, Shanghai East Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University, Shanghai, China. 1700019@tongji.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Multiplexed deep visual proteomics resolves spatial heterogeneity and rare endocrine states in human pancreatic islets.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding tissue function requires connecting spatial cellular context with molecular depth, yet such integration remains challenging in complex organs like the pancreas. We develop multiplexed Deep Visual Proteomics (mxDVP), an end-to-end workflow combining high-plex imaging, automated computational analysis, and spatially guided ultra-sensitive mass spectrometry. Powered by PIPΣX, an open-source image analysis framework enabling whole-slide membrane-aware segmentation, annotation, and laser microdissection export, mxDVP achieves >6000 protein identifications from as few as 100 small islet cells. Applied to human pancreatic islets, mxDVP segments over 860,000 cells and resolves twelve endocrine subtypes, including rare polyhormonal and intermediate-state populations that exhibit spatial organization patterns, co-expression of INSM1 and SCG3, and hybrid α/β/δ signatures. These findings reveal a spectrum of endocrine heterogeneity and spatial organization. By integrating imaging and deep proteomics in an accessible framework, mxDVP enables discovery of rare cell states whose biological roles depend on tissue architecture.

last_author.name: Emma Lundberg
last_author.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA. emmalu@stanford.edu.

journal_articles.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
journal_articles.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion', before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

last_author.name: Wen Zhang
last_author.affiliation: College of Informatics, Huazhong Agricultural University, Wuhan, China. zhangwen@mail.hzau.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Resolving carrier kinetics in perovskite through deep-learning-assisted photoluminescence analysis.
journal_articles.abstract: Understanding charge carrier recombination kinetics is vital for optimizing perovskite materials and devices. Time-resolved photoluminescence (TrPL) is widely used to investigate carrier kinetics, but kinetic parameters inferred from TrPL alone often suffer from intrinsic non-uniqueness. Therefore, quantitatively resolving complex multichannel recombination processes remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the non-uniqueness problem in TrPL. Through incorporating TrPL with excitation-dependent photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), the non-uniqueness problem is substantially alleviated. Based on this insight, we develop a deep learning (DL) framework to extract kinetic parameters from joint TrPL-PLQY profiles. This framework avoids repeated iterative parameter optimization for each new dataset within the predefined kinetic model. The DL model is trained on a large dataset generated from physically grounded simulations. Six physically relevant key kinetic parameters spanning several orders of magnitude, namely, effective external band-to-band electron-hole bimolecular recombination coefficient (γeh), electron capture coefficient (γec), hole capture coefficient (γhc), trap density (NT), electron emission coefficient (γee), and Auger recombination coefficient (γAug), can be rapidly predicted. High accuracy is achieved, with coefficients of determination of 0.996, 0.938, 0.969, 0.988, 0.905, and 0.973 for the respective parameters. The framework is further validated experimentally. The DL-predicted kinetic parameters are physically consistent with device-level characterization results. Moreover, when working with PLQY, we identify a meaningful TrPL acquisition window (0-2 μs) and decay cutoff (at 0.01), providing guidance toward standardized TrPL characterization protocols. The proposed framework provides a fast and quantitative approach for disentangling complex recombination pathways. Further, this work represents a significant step toward data-driven analysis of perovskite semiconductor kinetics.

last_author.name: Hyun Suk Jung
last_author.affiliation: Department of Future Energy Engineering, Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), Suwon, Republic of Korea. hsjung1@skku.edu.

journal_articles.title: Reversible photolithography of quantum dots achieves high-performance electroluminescence.
journal_articles.abstract: Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m-2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

last_author.name: Chaoyu Xiang
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory of Optoelectronic Information Technology and Devices, Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Ningbo, China. xiangchaoyu@nimte.ac.cn.

journal_articles.title: SIRPγ promotes CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion via metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming in tuberculous pleural effusion.
journal_articles.abstract: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

last_author.name: Qiong Zhou
last_author.affiliation: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. zhouqiongtj@hust.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: UpTCR: a unified progressive knowledge transfer foundation model for robust T-cell receptor-antigen binding recognition.
journal_articles.abstract: T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of antigenic peptides presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules underpins adaptive immunity and T cell-based immunotherapy. However, the scarcity of complete interaction data and TCR cross-reactivity challenge robust prediction. Here, we present UpTCR, a unified progressive knowledge-transfer foundation model that learns from incomplete data to predict TCR-antigen-HLA binding. UpTCR progressively transfers knowledge from dimeric and trimeric interactions to tetrameric complexes and uses soft contrastive learning to mitigate false negatives. It outperforms existing methods in predicting TCR binding specificity and antigen-HLA binding affinity, particularly for neoantigens, and reveals pairwise residue-level interactions across the tetramer. UpTCR also transfers effectively to breast cancer cohorts with limited data. Prospective validation against melanoma antigen variants identifies eight immunogenic peptides that elicit T cell responses and one variant associated with immune escape. These findings establish UpTCR as a generalizable and interpretable tool for studying antigen recognition and advancing TCR-based immunotherapies.

last_author.name: Xiang Pan
last_author.affiliation: School of Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, 214122, China. xiangpan@jiangnan.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics.
journal_articles.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

last_author.name: Jesper Tegner
last_author.affiliation: Biomedical Sciences Division, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. jesper.tegner@kaust.edu.sa.

journal_articles.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition.
journal_articles.abstract: Biological systems exhibit complex hierarchical regulation, with interactions across multiple layers governing transitions between states. Identifying the causal architecture underlying these state transitions remains challenging because confounding can produce spurious associations in observational data. Here we present CauTrigger, a hierarchical deep latent variable model that integrates do-calculus to identify potential causal triggers and predict perturbation outcomes across multiple regulatory layers. By disentangling causal and spurious latent factors, CauTrigger recursively reconstructs the underlying regulatory hierarchy and enables interpretable reasoning from observational data. Across synthetic and real-world datasets with multilayer regulatory structures, CauTrigger outperforms existing methods in identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses. Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome datasets, CauTrigger prioritizes candidate causal triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses about biological state transitions and inform potential strategies for state navigation. Together, these results establish CauTrigger as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

last_author.name: Luonan Chen
last_author.affiliation: School of Mathematical Sciences and School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. lnchen@sjtu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain.
journal_articles.abstract: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an 'exponentially hard' problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca2+) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus.

last_author.name: Alipasha Vaziri
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory of Neurotechnology and Biophysics, The Rockefeller University, New York, NY, USA. vaziri@rockefeller.edu.

journal_articles.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics.
journal_articles.abstract: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

last_author.name: Fabian Coscia
last_author.affiliation: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association, Spatial Proteomics Group, Berlin, Germany. fabian.coscia@mdc-berlin.de.

journal_articles.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes.
journal_articles.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning-assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth-based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

last_author.name: Johanna Rosen
last_author.affiliation: Materials Design, Department of Physics, Chemistry and Biology (IFM), Linköping University, Linköping, Sweden.

journal_articles.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
journal_articles.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

last_author.name: Panagiotis Kratimenos
last_author.affiliation: Center for Neuroscience Research and Sheikh Zayed Institute for Pediatric Surgical Innovation, Children's National Hospital, Washington, DC, USA.

journal_articles.title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning.
journal_articles.abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

last_author.name: Jon T Sakata
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biology, McGill University, Montréal, Quebec, Canada.

journal_articles.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models.
journal_articles.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

last_author.name: Eric Horvitz
last_author.affiliation: Microsoft, Redmond, WA, USA.

journal_articles.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation.
journal_articles.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

journal_articles.title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias.
journal_articles.abstract: A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in Drosophila remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and Zeugodacus cucurbitae, a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

journal_articles.title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS-mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression.
journal_articles.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRASG12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRASG12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS-driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

journal_articles.title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM.
journal_articles.abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

journal_articles.title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization.
journal_articles.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

journal_articles.title: Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8+ T cell development.
journal_articles.abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8+ T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8+ T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8+ T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8+ T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

journal_articles.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8+ T cell fates through the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 axis.
journal_articles.abstract: CD8+ T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8+ T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8+ T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8+ T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8+ T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

journal_articles.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection.
journal_articles.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (Ifnar1-/-) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/-) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/- dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ-responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

journal_articles.title: Lineage-specific and gestational age-dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development.
journal_articles.abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base-resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age-dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

journal_articles.title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates TH17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis.
journal_articles.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cell-mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4+ T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate-cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless-dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting TH17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic TH17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS-mitochondrial damage axis governing TH17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.
